Read the 2020-2026 NC death certifications

::: callout-note  

This assumes you have the original data saved in a subfolder called `data/all_death_files/yr2020-forward/`

::: 

## Fixed-width specfications

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| output: false
#| eval: true

suppressWarnings(library(tidyverse))
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(duckdb)
library(here)
library(glue)


rm(list = ls())

# change this path if your data is organized differently

here::i_am("death-certificates/01-import-nc-deaths.qmd")

```

Create the map function to read in the proper files

```{r}
#| label: get-file-list


import_list <- list.files("data/all_death_files/yr2020-forward", full.names = TRUE) |> 
  set_names(\(x) str_extract(x, "\\d{4}(?=\\D*$)")) |> 
  (\(x) x[order(names(x))])()

# import_list

```

Import death list then combine into one sorted data frame

```{r}
#| label: import-all-deaths

death_list <- map ( import_list , 
  function(x) {
    deaths <- read_fwf(
        file = x,
        col_positions = nc_death_cols_2020,
        col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),  # read everything as character not number or date
        na = c("", " ", "Blank"), 
        locale= locale(encoding="WINDOWS-1252")  # to fix <92> instead of apostrophes and remove warnings
    ) |> 
    clean_names() 
    
    return (deaths)
  }

)

ncdeaths <- list_rbind ( death_list, names_to = "file_year") |> 
  rowid_to_column ( var = "orig_rowid" ) 

# I checked, file year is always the same as dod_year

```
Save the original, un-cleaned and raw data into an RDS file. 

```{r}
#| label: save-raw-dataframe

saveRDS(ncdeaths, here("death-certificates/data/deaths_2020_to_2026_raw.RDS"))


```

## Minimal cleanup

1. Remove the 25 or so "Void" records: void == "1"

```{r}
#| label: remove-void-records

cleanup_deaths <- 
  ncdeaths |> 
  filter ( void == "0")


```

2. Remove always-empty and many of the race codes

```{r}
#| label: remove-empty-cols

empty_cols <- setdiff(
  names(cleanup_deaths),
  names(janitor::remove_empty(cleanup_deaths, which = "cols"))
)

print ( empty_cols)

cleanup_deaths <-
  cleanup_deaths |> 
  remove_empty( which = "cols")


```
Removed 26 columns


3. Deal with dates, age and human-readable id

I'm doing both of these at the same time, since I have to use the same date functions for both of them. 

```{r}
#| label: create-dates


cleanup_deaths <-
cleanup_deaths |> 
  mutate (
           dod_full = glue("{dod_yr}{dod_mo}{dod_dy}") |> as.character(), 
           dob_full = glue("{dob_yr}{dob_mo}{dob_dy}") |> as.character(), 
           death_id = glue("{dod_full}_{lname}_{gname}_{dob_full}"),
           dod = ymd(dod_full, quiet=TRUE), 
           dob = ymd(dob_full, quiet=TRUE),
           doi = ymd( glue("{doi_yr}{doi_mo}{doi_dy}") |> as.character(), quiet=TRUE),
           age_value = case_when ( agetype == "1" ~ as.integer(age),
                                   agetype %in% c("2",  "4", "5", "6") ~ as.integer(0) , 
                                   .default = NA_integer_),
          .after=orig_rowid
)



```


To check for duplicates:

```{r}

dup_ids <- cleanup_deaths$death_id[duplicated(cleanup_deaths$death_id)] |> unique()

cleanup_deaths |> 
  filter(death_id %in% dup_ids) |> 
  arrange(death_id)



```


There are 9 duplicated death_id columns. Most of these look like they are actually duplicated death certificates.  I'm not worrying about it. (Only one or two look like it's possible they are twins ("BABY") who were born and died at the same time). These won't a


4. Race and Hispanic origin recoding

The NCHS bridge is an old thing to handle multirace, and isn't really used. Almost always empty in this file.

To recode:

* Combine the race codes into the major groups. These are the race1 through race15 (the non-literal ones). It appears that they have already been coded as the race code when it's a literal. For example all of the ones that have a Native American literal also have Native American as "Y" . The major groups are:  race1 = white, race2= black, race3 = Native American or Alaska Native, race4-10 are Asian, race11-race14 are NHOPI . (Hawiian and Pacific Islander). race15 is unknown.  Each major group is 1 or 0 

* To create the race code, anyone with sum of > 1 is multiracial; anyone with sum of 0 is unknown; otherwise, use the race

```{r}
#| label: create-race-collapse

cleanup_deaths <- cleanup_deaths |> 
  mutate(
    # one 1/0 flag per major group
    race_white = as.integer(race1 %in% "Y"),
    race_black = as.integer(race2 %in% "Y"),
    race_aian  = as.integer(race3 %in% "Y"),
    race_asian = as.integer(if_any(num_range("race", 4:10), \(x) x %in% "Y")),
    race_nhopi = as.integer(if_any(num_range("race", 11:14), \(x) x %in% "Y")),
    
    # how many major groups each person is in (race15, unknown, isn't counted)
    race_count = race_white + race_black + race_aian + race_asian + race_nhopi,
    
    race = factor(
      case_when(
        race_count > 1   ~ "Multiracial",
        race_count == 0  ~ "Unknown",
        race_white == 1  ~ "White",
        race_black == 1  ~ "Black",
        race_aian  == 1  ~ "American Indian or Alaska Native",
        race_asian == 1  ~ "Asian",
        race_nhopi == 1  ~ "Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander"
      ) , 
    levels = c("White", "Black", "AIAN", "Asian", "NHOPI", "Multiracial", "Unknown")
    ), 

    hispanic = as.integer(if_any(num_range("dethnic", 1:4), \(x) x %in% "H" ) ), 
    nonhispanic = as.integer(if_all(num_range("dethnic", 1:4), \(x) x %in% "N") ), 
    
    ethnicity = factor ( case_when (  hispanic == 1 ~ "Hispanic", nonhispanic==1 ~"Non-Hispanic", .default = "Unknown") , 
                            levels = c("Hispanic", "Non-Hispanic", "Unknown") ) 
  )

```




5. Create convenience column for names and addresses

This includes mother, decedent . It doesn't appear that the father's full name exists in the dataset - the column that would have had it is always empty. The father's last name is the only part of the name that we have. 

This is kind of weird - we have the father's last name, but not the father's first name. We have the mother's first and middle name, and her maiden name, but not her last name. It doesn't really take into account complicated family relationships. 

However, it seemst that never-married women's names are there. It's unclear what happens if the decedent's mother was married more than once. However, I'll just keep it as the mother's "maiden" name, but put the father's name right next to it. 

The only zip codes that are > 5 characters are the unknown ones

```{r}
#| label: combine-names

cleanup_deaths <- cleanup_deaths |> 
  unite(decedent_given, gname, mname, suff, 
        sep = " ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  unite(decedent_name, lname, decedent_given, 
        sep = ", ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  
  unite(mother_given, dmomf, dmommid, 
        sep = " ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  unite(mother_name, dmommdn, mother_given, 
        sep = ", ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  
  
  # don't use the unit number - too complicated, and rarely used.
  unite(res_street, stnum_r, predir_r, stname_r, stdesig_r, postdir_r,
        sep = " ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  unite(death_street, stnum_d, predir_d, stname_d, stdesig_d, postdir_d, 
        sep = " ", na.rm = TRUE, remove = FALSE) |> 
  mutate(across( c(decedent_name, mother_name, res_street, death_street) , \(x) na_if( x, "" )
                ) , 
         across( c(zip9_d, zip9_r) , \(x) str_replace(x, "999999999", "UNKNOWN") 
               )
    )

```


## Apply code translations 

Import the lookup tables that I saved in the program `all_death_files/certificates-translation-codes.R`, which is saved as `death-cert-translation-codes-2020.RDS`
This is a list of named vectors, with the name of the column as the name of the list item. 

```{r}
#| label: lookup-tables

translation_codes <- readRDS(here("death-certificates/data/all_death_files/death-cert-translation-codes-2020.RDS"))
# remove "codes" from the end of the vector names.
names(translation_codes) <- str_remove(names(translation_codes), "_codes$")

```

Apply all of the lookup codes to create factors instead of character values -- better for making summary charts, etc.  First create a function that can be called

```{r}
#| label: code-translation-function

# code =  the name of the code value
# translation map = named vector for translation
# took out ",  .names  = "{.col}_lit"" from mutate - already keeping original

code_to_factor <- function(x, codes) {
  codes  <- unlist(codes)                                  # back to a named vector
  codes <- unlist(codes)
  factor(as.character(x),
         levels  = names(codes),               # the original codes 
         labels  = paste(names(codes), codes, sep = " - "),   # what to show: 
         ordered = TRUE)
}



translated_deaths <- cleanup_deaths |>
  mutate(across(any_of(names(translation_codes)),
                \(x) code_to_factor(x, translation_codes[[cur_column()]])
              )
  )

```


## Save cleaned up data

Get rid of columns I don't plan to save in this iteration, remembering that I still have the originals for things like addresses and names parts. For the purpose of searching, though, it's easier to have the combined ones. 

```{r}
#| label: move-columns

deaths_save <-
  translated_deaths |> 
  select  (
      orig_rowid, 
      death_id,
      dod_yr,
      dod,
      tod,
      decedent_name,
      dob,
      age_value,
      sex,
      manner,
      acme_uc,
      rac,
      referred,
      autop,
      autopf,
      dplace,
      dinsti,
#      address_d,
      death_street,
      citytext_d,
      zip9_d,
      countytext_d,
      res_street,
      unitnum_r,
      citytext_r,
      statec,
      zip9_r, 
      countytext_r,
      bplace_cnt,
      bplace_st,
      race,
      ethnicity,
      marital,
      deduc,
      mother_name,
      flname,
      occup,
      disp,
      injpl,
      howinj,
  ) |> 
   mutate(
      fix_home = dod_yr == "2020" & str_starts(dplace, "4") & is.na(death_street),
      death_street = if_else(fix_home, dinsti, death_street),
      dinsti   = if_else(fix_home, "HOME", dinsti)
  ) |> 
  select (-fix_home)








```

# save to duckdb and RDS

```{r}
#| label: setup-duckdb

con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), here("death-certificates/data/deaths2020up.duckdb"))
dbWriteTable(con,  "deaths_cleaned_2020", deaths_save, overwrite=TRUE)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown=TRUE)


# rds will keep factors and dates right
saveRDS(deaths_save, here("death-certificates/data/deaths_cleaned_2020_to_2026.RDS"))


```
